why: A link checker fails open in silence: a form it does not read, a finding it drops, or a run over no files all look exactly like a tree whose links resolve. These representative edits cover inline-link matching, missing targets, the empty-run refusal, and the path the verdict takes to the exit code; they do not exhaust link forms, anchors or quoting rules.

mutations.name: the inline-link pattern stops matching
mutations.breaks: The oldest rule here, disabled by a regex that no longer fires. Every inline link reads clean because none is seen.

mutations.name: a missing target is not a problem
mutations.breaks: The file is resolved, found not to exist, and the finding is thrown away — the check runs and reports nothing.

mutations.name: a run that found no files reports clean
mutations.breaks: Nothing to check and checked-and-clean are different answers. A checker that can pass by having nothing to look at is not a gate.

mutations.name: the findings are computed and then reported as clean
mutations.breaks: Every rule above works and the verdict never reaches the exit code. This is why the self-test goes through main() rather than calling check() and reading its list.
mutations.find:
print(f"check-doc-links: {len(problems)} broken link(s) in {len(files)} file(s)", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
mutations.replace:
print(f"check-doc-links: {len(problems)} broken link(s) in {len(files)} file(s)", file=sys.stderr)
        return 0
